extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection via unsanitized `name` parameter — Remote code execution on the server via Jinja2 SSTI payloads (e.g. `{{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}`), and disclosure of hardcoded secrets (SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN, SUPER_SECRET_NAME) via template introspection. [verified: User-controlled `name` is embedded into the raw string before Template() is constructed and then .render() is called, so Jinja syntax in `name` is compiled and executed with no sanitization anywhere in the flow.]

Reflected XSS via unescaped `name` parameter — Attacker-crafted link causes arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser session (session/cookie theft, phishing, actions on behalf of the user). [verified: Even setting aside SSTI, `name` is spliced unescaped into HTML then returned as HTMLResponse, and Template().render() performs no auto-escaping (no Environment autoescape configured), so `<script>` payloads execute in the victim browser.]

Hardcoded secret token in source code — Anyone with read access to the repository (or a leaked build artifact) obtains the secret token, which may be used elsewhere in the system for authentication or as a shared secret, enabling impersonation or bypass of controls relying on its secrecy. [verified: SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN is a literal hardcoded string in version-controlled source with a FIXME showing it should come from env, so anyone with repo/source access obtains the secret.]

Debug mode enables verbose error disclosure — Stack traces and internal application state (variable values, file paths, potentially secrets in scope) exposed to unauthenticated attackers when an exception occurs. [verified: config.DEBUG is read directly from environment and passed to FastAPI(debug=...) with no override, so if set truthy in any deployment, unauthenticated clients get verbose tracebacks on exceptions (e.g. from the requests.get call).]
